packages.description:
ADR 0005 §3.1, §3.9, §15.1.

- Pin Node 26.12.1 in .nvmrc, set `engines.node` to `>=26.12.0`, and make CI use .nvmrc.
- Pin exactly, choosing the newest release at least 7 days old and recording the choice in the ADR §3 tables: `@atproto/oauth-client-node` 0.5.10, `ws` 8.22.0, `@types/ws`, `undici` 8.12.2 (it must equal `process.versions.undici`), `fflate`, `esbuild` 0.28.2 (direct devDependency), `lastfm-ts-api` 2.6.2 (dev only, the real-client e2e) and `@types/node` 26.x. Regenerate package-lock.json.
- Add the `worker-node` vitest project in worker/vitest.node.config.ts: `environment: 'node'`, `include: ['test/node/**/*.test.ts']`, `sequence.groupOrder: 1`. Exclude `test/node/**` from worker/vitest.modules.config.ts.
- Switch packages/core to `environment: 'node'`; its 34 tests must pass unchanged under Node's ICU (Unicode 17).
- worker/tsconfig.json gains `node` types next to `@cloudflare/workers-types`. If the two conflict, move the Workers-only files (src/index.ts, src/do/index-do.ts, src/scheduled.ts, src/env.ts) into worker/tsconfig.workers.json until N7-01 deletes them.
- scripts/check-ts.sh gains two steps that run when their file exists: `npx tsx scripts/check-node-bundle.ts` (the Node bundle guard, a new file from N3-07; the existing Workers `check-bundle.ts` step stays until N7-01) and `npx tsx scripts/build-server.ts --check` (N3-07). Wiring them here means no later package edits check-ts.sh before N7-01.
- **Runtime-neutral core checks (ADR §15.3).** packages/core/test/unicode-runtime.test.ts asserts `navigator.userAgent === 'Cloudflare-Workers'` at :257 and :364, which is `Node.js/26` under Node. Replace both assertions, keeping every title: ICU reports Unicode 17 or newer (`process.versions.unicode`), and the NFKC oracle drift is 0 code points outside the documented unassigned set. The UA check is recorded as a named change in node-port-inventory.json by N2-02.
- **Timeouts.** worker/vitest.node.config.ts keeps vitest's default 5 s test timeout. Tests never wait for production durations (busy timeout, drain window and alarms are injected, ADR §3.2, §3.10); process-level tests live in scripts/test with explicit timeouts.
- **Gate duration (ADR §15.1).** check-ts.sh accepts `--projects <list>`, used only by the nested negative controls in scripts/test/check-ts.test.ts so that each control runs just the project it exercises instead of a full nested gate (the existing nested run already takes 91.6 s of its 180 s budget). It writes work/gate-durations.json with one duration per step. No large-fixture suite may live under worker/test/node/**; those belong to worker-bench.

Only this package regenerates the lockfile in wave 0. Later packages that add or remove dependencies own package-lock.json in their own wave.

ADR 0005 §5.7, §6.1–§6.3, §7, §8, §16.

- **lexicons/scrobble.json:** add the §6.2 optional fields with their limits. Nothing else changes; no field becomes required.

Remove the static client-metadata asset row and document the dynamic /oauth/client-metadata.json and /oauth/jwks.json.
- **docs/planning/API.md:** add the v1.2 amendment paragraph; narrow 'no route reads a session' to 'no v1.1 read route'.
- **docs/planning/AMENDMENTS-node.md:** B1–B20 issue-amendment texts in the AMENDMENTS-workers.md format, including the TESTING.md harness wording (B10), a machine-readable "Superseded ADR 0004 amendments" list for the validator, and per-leaf sections naming the cases retired under B4 and B11.
- **docs/compat/lastfm.md and docs/compat/listenbrainz.md:** the client-facing protocol specifications of §7 and §8: methods, parameters, errors and client setup for Pano, multi-scrobbler, Web Scrobbler, Navidrome, Jellyfin and Music Assistant. lastfm.md states that lastfm-ts-api clients such as multi-scrobbler must use `https://music.214510.xyz/2.0/` and cannot use the loopback address or any non-443 port; that `/api/auth` and `/api/auth/` both work; and that `library.removeScrobble` with no match answers 7. listenbrainz.md states that Web Scrobbler supports scrobbles and now playing only (its love and unlove call api.listenbrainz.org with the user's token, so users must not use love with the custom entry and must revoke the token if they did), and documents the deviations: a 400 only for input ListenBrainz itself rejects; listens up to +3,600 s accepted and those beyond +300 s written once they become valid (listened_at − 300 s); names that ListenBrainz accepts but our validator refuses answered 200, not written, and listed in GET /api/v1/account/ignored-listens; -1 clears a love; return_msid only for playing_now.
- **ADR 0002 and ADR 0004:** status lines say which sections ADR 0005 supersedes.
- **scripts/validate_case_map.py:** accept test ids declared in docs/planning/node-waves.json as well as workers-waves.json (new `--node-waves` option, default path). **Pending targets (ADR §15.3):** with `--check-tests --node-wave <n>`, a mapped target declared by a node-waves package of a wave later than n is reported as `pending (wave <m>, <package id>)` and does not fail; targets of waves ≤ n must exist with their title. Reject every retirement that cites an amendment AMENDMENTS-node.md lists as superseded (A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A11, A12, A15, A16, A18, A19 and D), and accept `retired:B<n>` when that B amendment's section in AMENDMENTS-node.md names the case.
- **docs/verification/ts-case-map.json (ADR §15.3, §20.2):** of the 43 cases retired under superseded amendments (26 under A1, A3, A11, A12, A15 and A19, 14 under D, 3 under A4), un-retire the 39 whose reasons ADR 0005 made false and map each to the named test listed in ADR §20.2; re-retire M1.2.3/static_elf and M6.4.1/static_release under B11 and M1.2.1/locked_build and M1.2.1/dependency_direction under B4 with reasons that are true on Node. The map then validates in this wave, because every target is declared in node-waves.json.
- **scripts/validate_contracts.py:** validate love.json, check that every scrobble.json property other than the required four is optional, and check the new examples against their schemas.

**Retire workers-backend.sh from the gate (ADR §2.2, §15.3).** It stays on disk until N7-01 deletes it, but from wave 0 it is no longer run: its `--check-tests` step fails as soon as the 39 cases point at tests of later waves, and its Playwright step drives the browser OAuth client that N5-01 removes. AMENDMENTS-node.md (B10 section) states this.

**scripts/acceptance/node-interim.sh --wave <n> --out <dir>** is the per-wave acceptance until N8-01: check-ts (npm run check), the Python case-map regressions, `validate_case_map.py --check-tests --node-wave <n>`, check_goldens.sh, the live no-env checks, and Playwright only when n ≥ 6. packages.title: IndexCore extraction, Host interface, AppServices, extension timers
packages.description:
ADR 0005 §2.2, §3.1, §3.3.

- **IndexCore.** Move the IndexDO body (index-do.ts:276-600) into `IndexCore(config, host: Host, extensions: CoreExtension[])`. `Host` is `{db, alarm, extensionAlarm, connectJetstream, transport, backup?, log, clock, random}`. index-do.ts becomes a thin wrapper that builds a Workers Host and delegates, so the workerd suites keep passing.
- **Every non-class export moves too (ADR §2.2).** `envLogger`, `createLogger`, `LogSink`, `INDEX_NAME`, `GC_*`, `HINT_*`, `ALARM_SLICE_MS`, `PITR_WINDOW_MS`, `PITR_RESTART_DELAY_MS`, `ADMIN_RESNAPSHOT_REASON`, `IndexDeps`, `NotReadyError`, `IndexError` and its constants, `GcReport` and `runGc` move to worker/src/app/index-core.ts, which imports nothing from cloudflare:* or env.ts values (types only through `import type`; `envLogger` takes a structural `{CURSOR_KEY?, ADMIN_TOKEN?}`). index-do.ts re-exports all of them, so router.ts, http/admin.ts and every test keep compiling, and keeps `protected buildDeps(env, ctx): IndexDeps` as the override seam for the test entries until N4-03 and N7-01.
- **IndexRpc** (contracts.ts) gains `adminBackup()`. `adminPitr` stays until N7-01, and a host without a backup or PITR port answers `not_supported`.
- **AppServices** (worker/src/app/services.ts) is an empty interface that features extend by declaration merging.
- **Timers** (timers.ts): `TIMER_NAMES` stays exactly the seven core names, so worker/test/storage/timers.test.ts (owned by N1-10 in this wave; it schedules every TIMER_NAMES entry at :261-272) needs no change. A new `EXTENSION_TIMER_NAMES` holds outbox, forward, import, oauth-keepalive, expiry-sweep and backup, in that order. A name with no handler is never armed. A throwing handler is re-armed with backoff.
- **Two lanes (ADR §3.3).** `runDue`, `armAlarm`, `nextDue`, `recoverOrphans` and the claim step take a lane `{names}` that defaults to `TIMER_NAMES`; each reads and writes only its lane's names and their `~running:` rows (today `nextDue` ~l.186-193 and `recoverOrphans` ~l.262-271 read every known name). The single-flight guard stays keyed on the storage object, so IndexCore drives `TIMER_NAMES` from `Host.alarm` and `EXTENSION_TIMER_NAMES` from `Host.extensionAlarm`; neither lane waits for, recovers or reschedules the other's timers.
- **AlarmStorage** becomes the structural `{setAlarm(ms), deleteAlarm()}` type, so timers.ts no longer needs @cloudflare/workers-types (N7-01 then does not touch it).
- **worker/test/harness/local-index.ts:** METHODS gains `adminBackup` (it is `Record<keyof IndexRpc, true>`, so tsc -b would fail without it). N7-01 removes `adminPitr` from it.

packages.title: Pinned outbound transport and policyFetch for POST and non-SafeFetch traffic
packages.description:
ADR 0005 §3.5.

The transport lives in worker/src/node/ (ADR §3.5): @atmusic/atproto is Workers- and browser-safe with no Node built-ins and declares no undici, while worker-node already has Node types and N0-01 pins undici in worker/package.json.

**pinned-transport.ts:** `pinnedTransport({lookup?, caps})` returns a Transport over an undici Agent built with `connect: {rejectUnauthorized: true, lookup}`, whose lookup applies `isAllowedAddress` (net/url-policy.ts) to every answer and connects only to the checked address. Failures are `TransportError {code: 'blocked_address'|'dns'|'connect'|'timeout'|'too_large'|'redirect'|'unpinned_fetch'}`, never a raw TypeError. It also exports `unpinnedFetchStub`, which run() installs as globalThis.fetch (N3-07).

**SafeFetch is not changed** (packages/atproto/src/net/safe-fetch.ts stays GET-only, read-kind-only, with its DoH pre-check, decision recorded in ADR §3.5); it runs over the pinned transport.

**policy-fetch.ts:** `policyFetch(input, init, {caps})` is fetch-shaped for every other request, including POST: the URL policy (https only, default port, no IP literal, forbidden suffixes), `redirect: 'manual'` with every 3xx a TransportError, a 10 s deadline, a request-body cap and a response-body cap, and TransportError for every failure. No DoH; pinning is its address check. The OAuth client (N2-03), PdsWriter (N2-05), the forward clients (N3-08) and the import sources (N3-09) use it.

Tests inject the lookup function and the socket connector (a spy that records the address it was asked to connect to and answers from an in-memory duplex), so no real socket, DNS query or network is used; policyFetch tests run over the same injected connector.

packages.title: Confidential atproto OAuth client: identity adapter, metadata, JWKS, keyset, non-throwing encrypted stores, re-sign-in, reconciliation, keepalive
packages.description:
ADR 0005 §5.2–§5.5, §5.7.

**oauth-client.ts:** NodeOAuthClient with requestLocalLock, `fetch: policyFetch` (N1-05), `identityResolver` from identity-adapter.ts, and query response mode. Never `handleResolver` alone: the library would build its own DidResolver against https://plc.directory/ and run it with noCache in verifyIssuer on every token response and refresh.
- `authorize(handle, {bindingHash})` stores the login-CSRF cookie hash in oauth_states.session_binding; `callback(params, {bindingHash})` refuses a mismatch before the code exchange and consumes the state (ADR §5.6); `restore(did)` and `revoke(did)`.
- **Hooks (ADR §5.2):** onSessionUpdated sets accounts.oauth_status='active' and moves the DID's blocked operations back to queued; onSessionDeleted sets reauth_required and blocks them, **except** while the callback wrapper's per-sub in-callback flag is set, when the library's own `revoke(sub)` of the previous session only deletes the old row.
- **Binding check (ADR §5.5):** a definite issuer or handle mismatch revokes the new session (403 oauth_binding_mismatch); an identity-resolution error revokes nothing, keeps the new session, sets no cookie and surfaces 502 oauth_upstream.
- Each OAuth case the Workers map retired under A3 or D is mapped to a test here (ADR §20.2).

**identity-adapter.ts:** the library's IdentityResolver over our identity.resolveDid and identity.resolveHandle, mapping `noCache: true` to `{fresh: true}`.

**oauth-stores.ts:** the state and session SimpleStores over oauth_states and oauth_sessions with AES-GCM sealing and AAD, a single-use 600 s state, and client_kid recorded. **No CAS** (ADR §5.5): `set()` writes unconditionally and increments generation, and **never throws** for a storage failure: the session is kept in an in-memory write-behind map that get() reads first, `oauth_store_write_failed` is logged without secrets, `oauth_store_degraded` is raised for readiness and adminStatus, and the write is retried on each get, set and keepalive run.

**reconcile.ts (ADR §5.5):** `reconcileSignInPolicy(m, policy)`, run at startup and by expiry-sweep (both wired by N4-01 features): for each account the policy refuses, revoke and delete the OAuth session, delete web sessions and protocol credentials (journaled through Revocations, N1-08), set links revoked, block queued operations, set signed_out.

**keepalive.ts:** the `oauth-keepalive` timer: refresh sessions last refreshed over 30 days ago, at most 20 per run, only for DIDs in use (live web session, a credential with last_used_ms within 90 days, an active link, a queued, running or blocked operation, or an unfinished import job); others are revoked upstream and marked signed_out. It pauses while the injected `diskLow()` predicate (N1-07 disk.ts) is true.

**client-metadata.ts:** the exact §5.3 documents, with client_name from packages/core/src/client-name.ts (`CLIENT_NAME = 'AT Protocol Music'`, moved from scripts/gen-config.ts:42; N5-01 switches gen-config to import it). **keyset.ts:** keys from secrets plus announced public keys.

packages.title: Last.fm protocol core: parameters, method-scoped signatures, errors, XML/JSON encoding with list elements
packages.description:
ADR 0005 §7.1, §7.2, §7.4, §7.6.

- **params.ts:** query plus form body; duplicate refusal; indexed arrays 0–49 and the unindexed form; format negotiation (query, body, Accept).
- **signature.ts:** byte-ordered sign and verify, excluding api_sig, format and callback; constant-time comparison; the known-pair, issued-key and unknown-key policy. **The policy applies only to methods whose ADR §7.5 Auth column contains sig** (`requiresSignature(method)`); for read methods api_sig is ignored whether present, absent or wrong (ADR §7.3).
- **errors.ts:** the code, message and HTTP table.
- **encode.ts:** the element tree to XML (escape, strip invalid characters, raw) and to JSON (the §7.2 rules). Elements carry a `list` flag: a flagged child always serialises as a JSON array, including `[]` and a one-element array. Only scrobbles.scrobble keeps the single-child-becomes-object quirk. JSON number exceptions: scrobbles.@attr accepted/ignored, user.registered.#text and session.subscriber.

packages.title: ListenBrainz protocol core: validation that rejects only what ListenBrainz rejects, token header, errors, credential-first limits, CORS
packages.description:
ADR 0005 §8.1–§8.3, §8.7.

- **validate.ts:** `validateSubmission(rawBody, now)` performs the envelope checks in ListenBrainz's order with verbatim messages, then the per-listen checks with ListenBrainz's own bounds (listened_at ≤ now + 3,600 s). Only those produce an error (a 400 later). It then classifies each valid listen: `accept` (within our +300 s and our scrobble validator), `defer` with `notBeforeMs = (listened_at − 300) s` when now + 300 s < listened_at ≤ now + 3,600 s, or `ignore` with reason artist_invalid or track_invalid when a name fails our validator (more than 256 scalars, malformed UTF-16) but passes ListenBrainz's checks. The output is `{listens: [{record, disposition}]}` or the first ListenBrainz-level error.
- **auth-header.ts:** scheme parsing and the 401 messages.
- **errors.ts:** `{code, error}` bodies and CORS headers.
- **rate-headers.ts:** the X-RateLimit-* header set.
- **limiter.ts (ADR §8.7):** `limit(req, tokenResult)`: a request with a valid token is charged to its per-token bucket only (refuse mode); an unauthenticated request or a failed token check is charged to the per-IP bucket keyed by `rateKeyOf` in an `evict-lru` BucketSet (N1-06). An authenticated request is never refused because the per-IP set is full.

packages.title: Auth routes: start, callback, session, logout, disconnect, client metadata and JWKS
packages.description:
ADR 0005 §5.3, §5.6, §5.7. auth/start enforces exactly one Origin, applies the sign-in policy to the handle-resolved DID, and sets `__Host-atmusic_oauth` (32 random bytes, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ because the __Host- prefix requires it, Max-Age=600), passing its SHA-256 to N2-03. The callback requires the cookie, clears it, applies the sign-in policy to the session sub (403 signin_not_allowed: the session is revoked upstream and nothing is stored), then calls `admit(db, did, 'notify', now)`; queue_full is left to the import timer and the outbox (ADR §5.7, §11.2). These routes self-register as RouteDef[] and are wired in N4-01. Tests mount them with test/node/support/app.ts against fake-oauth-as, fake-pds and fake-plc.

**Round 2.** `DELETE /api/v1/account/connection` (cookie plus CSRF, ADR §5.7): revoke and delete the OAuth session upstream, delete every web session, Last.fm session, app password, ListenBrainz token and issued app of the DID, delete its linked accounts (their forward rows cascade), cancel its not-yet-sent operations, journal every deletion, set signed_out, clear the cookie, 204. The callback maps a binding-check identity error to 502 oauth_upstream without revoking (N2-03).

packages.description:
ADR 0005 §3.9–§3.11, §14.5. The process half of the round-1 N2-01.

- **run.ts / main.ts (ADR §3.9, §3.10).** `run(opts): Promise<ExitCode>` is side-effect free on import and takes argv, env, clock, exit, `busyTimeoutMs` and `drainMs` (production 5000 and 25000 from NodeConfig). Order: `checkRuntimeEnv` (exit 78 naming the variable), config and secrets (78), install `unpinnedFetchStub` as globalThis.fetch, open the db (exclusive lock; 75 database_locked; 78 for a missing file without `--init`), the admin socket, the pre-migration backup (free-space check, 78 naming ATMUSIC_MIN_FREE_BYTES when it fails) and migration under EXTEND_TIMEOUT_USEC, compose (N2-01), listen (LISTEN_FDS, then ATMUSIC_LISTEN, then 127.2.0.1:8888), READY=1. `--version` prints the build-time git sha; `--check-config` validates and exits. main.ts is the only module with a top-level effect: it calls run() with the process values and exits.
- **shutdown.ts:** the SIGTERM drain with the injected drain window.
- **systemd.ts:** READY=1, STOPPING=1, WATCHDOG=1 and EXTEND_TIMEOUT_USEC through an injectable systemd-notify spawner.
- **admin-socket.ts and http/admin.ts:** the socket routes (status with backup age, queue depths, upload-directory bytes, free space, low_disk and oauth_store_degraded; backup; resnapshot; oauth prune-kid) with the portable constant-time compare. The Workers TCP admin route and ADMIN_TOKEN stay in ROUTES until N4-03 ports composition/admin.test.ts; N7-01 deletes them.
- **backup.ts:** refuse unless free ≥ db size + ATMUSIC_MIN_FREE_BYTES (failed backup_runs row, error low_disk); node:sqlite async `backup(db, tmp, {rate})`; integrity_check in a worker_thread on a read-only connection to the copy; rename and fsync; backup_runs with kind; retention 7 daily and 4 weekly over daily and manual runs only; the pre-migration backup; the `backup` extension timer; after a completed backup, `revocations.truncateBefore(oldest backup file time)` (N1-08).
- **build-server.ts:** esbuild bundles worker/dist/node/main.mjs, with `--check` and the git sha embedded; `--e2e [--entry <path>]` builds worker/dist/node/e2e.mjs from worker/test/e2e/node-entry.ts (which imports run.ts, never main.ts; N6-01) and exits 2 when the entry is missing. Both builds write metafiles.
- **check-node-bundle.ts (new file; check-bundle.ts is untouched for deploy.sh and deploy.test.ts until N7-01):** fails on main.mjs inputs under test-support, worker/test or router-transport, on com.example.atmusic handling, on a cloudflare: import, on an input worker/src/do/index-do.ts, worker/src/scheduled.ts, worker/src/env.ts, worker/src/index.ts or worker/src/router.ts, on a crypto-build mismatch, and on an unpinned fetch path (any input other than pinned-transport.ts, policy-fetch.ts and the four documented fallback sites referencing globalThis.fetch, a bare fetch( or fetchTransport; or a production createIdentityResolver, createHandleResolver, createSafeFetch or new NodeOAuthClient call without its transport or fetch property). Fixture options are found by a comment-stripped call-site scan of the production sources (`fixtureOrigins: true`, `fixture: true` passed as an option, routerTransport, fixtureTransport, test-support imports, fixedClock, seededRandom), as worker/test/acceptance/security.test.ts:392-407 does, with a non-vacuity check (at least 60 files scanned, the `fixtureOrigins?: boolean` parameter found in worker/src/node/config.ts). When e2e.mjs exists, every worker/src and packages/*/src input of main.mjs except worker/src/node/main.ts must be an e2e.mjs input with the same hash, and e2e.mjs may add only worker/test/e2e, worker/test/node/support and test-support inputs. It prints the git sha and the bundle SHA-256. N0-01 already wired it into check-ts.sh.

**Tests.** worker-node tests drive run() and shutdown() in-process with injected exit, clock, busyTimeoutMs ≈ 200 and drainMs ≈ 200. Tests that need a real second process spawn the built main.mjs from scripts/test/build-server.test.ts with explicit 60 s timeouts; nothing spawns tsx.

packages.title: Imports: Last.fm and ListenBrainz sources, uploads, ZIP bounds, staging, dedupe, writer, routes
packages.description:
ADR 0005 §11.

**Job states:** waiting_index → fetching → writing → done, plus paused, failed and cancelled. Driven by the `import` extension timer.

**Sources:**
- Last.fm backward paging (fixed `to`, boundary dedupe, progress guarantee, nowplaying skip, sk when linked). It uses the shared upstream pacing from N3-08 through an injected `Pacer` interface defined here, so the two packages share no file.
- ListenBrainz max_ts paging.
- Uploads (64 MiB, streamed to disk at 0600, 507 past ATMUSIC_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES or below ATMUSIC_MIN_FREE_BYTES; deleted once parsed or when the job is cancelled or fails; a startup sweep removes orphans). Parsing is streaming only (ADR §11.1): fflate Unzip with UnzipInflate, line-by-line JSONL, a page-splitting tokenizer for the Last.fm JSON export, and bomb bounds on actual inflated bytes (64 MiB per entry, 256 MiB total).
- ListenBrainz feedback.jsonl resolution against the archive listens (recording_msid, then recording_mbid via mbid_mapping or additional_info), after all listens entries.

**Pipeline:**
- staging with listen-key dedupe;
- the writer creating import-priority operations in slices of 1,000;
- feedback score 1 → love.put operations with origin import, scores 0 and -1 skipped, unresolved rows invalid with reason feedback_unresolved;
- the crash-loop guard: import_jobs.attempts incremented and committed before each slice, reset on completion, failed with crash_loop at 3;
- admission: a waiting_index job whose DID has no users row retries `admit(…, 'notify', …)` on each import timer run with backoff (ADR §11.2).
- staging rows deleted 7 days after done.

**Routes:** POST imports, POST imports/upload, GET list and detail with ETA, cancel, resume.

**Round 2.** The Last.fm and ListenBrainz import sources fetch through policyFetch (N1-05). The writer pauses while diskLow() (N1-07) is true, and resumes when space returns.

packages.title: Production feature wiring and in-process journeys
packages.description:
